question: Indicate among the following the most probable complication that presents the patient operated on, 20 years ago, of gastric ulcer by means of antrectomy and gastrojejunostomy (Billroth II) that comes to his office referring to post-radial abdominal pain, abdominal distension, diarrhea and analytical data of malabsorption of fats and vitamin B12:

options.opd: Afferent loop syndrome with bacterial overgrowth.

analysis: The patient's symptoms of post-prandial abdominal pain, distension, diarrhea, malabsorption of fats and vitamin B12, along with a history of antrectomy and gastrojejunostomy (Billroth II), are suggestive of afferent loop syndrome with bacterial overgrowth. This condition can lead to malabsorption of nutrients, including fats and vitamin B12, and can present with the described symptoms.
